abstract: The users of electricity networks are organized into groups where the production and consumption of electricity is in balance. The study examines the formation of these balancing groups using a cooperative game in partition function form defined over an ideal (lossless) DC load flow model of the power grid. The games contain widespread externalities that can be both negative and positive. The stability of certain partitions is studied using the concept of the recursive core. While the game is clearly cohesive, it is not necessarily superadditive, and subadditivity may be a barrier to achieve full cooperation.
summary_en: Electricity markets feature 'balancing groups' where production and consumption must net to zero in real time. Csercsik and Kóczy model the formation of these groups as a cooperative game in partition-function form on a DC load-flow grid. Externalities run in both directions (positive AND negative), making analysis non-trivial. They study stability via the recursive core and find the game is cohesive but not necessarily superadditive — meaning subadditivity can prevent full cooperation across the grid. Useful framework for understanding how voluntary balancing groups stabilise (or fail to stabilise) in liberalised electricity markets.
data_used: Theoretical model — cooperative game in partition function form over DC load-flow electrical grid. No primary dataset.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for MEKH and MAVIR when designing Hungarian balance-group rules and incentives. The paper shows full grid-wide cooperation is not automatic when subadditivity holds — useful diagnostic for evaluating Hungarian and EU electricity-market integration mechanisms.
title: Efficiency and stability in electrical power transmission networks: A partition function form approach
